BLOCKER: main.go calls `store.OpenWithPool(...)`, `store.PoolOptions` and `(*PgStore).Stats()`, but this change set contains no `product-forge/go/store` edits; if those APIs are not already shipped, the build and `go test ./...` fail and the AC is unmet — include the store-side change or prove it pre-exists.
MAJOR: Shutdown drains for `max(30s, WriteTimeout)` = 180s, not the AC's 30s; docs §10 and the acceptance criteria now disagree on the drain budget (who may SIGKILL when, when the pool closes).

`auditCoverage` is the only handler whose context-setup line is untouched; if it still derives from `context.Background()`, client disconnect/deadline does not cancel its coverage DB read (AC: every handler uses r.Context()/dbCtx).

Quota slots are acquired before the body is read and Go body reads are not context-aware; an unauthenticated slow-body client (quota runs before auth) can pin all 10 global slots for up to ReadTimeout (180s), turning the anti-evasion control into an availability surface.

Effective defaults now exist in three unsynchronised places (`config/env-flags.json`, `limits.DefaultConfig()`, docs §10) with no test asserting they agree — drift silently ships wrong production limits.
MINOR: `/artifacts/` (download) is not classified as upload: it gets the 30s JSON timeout (large artifact downloads can 504) and is metered under `class="json"`, skewing the 413/429/504-per-class metrics.
`/metrics` is blocked by the role gate, so counters/pool saturation become unobservable exactly when the service fails closed.
`/metrics` exposes histograms, contradicting the AC's "counters only"; docs describe histograms instead — AC vs shipped contract diverge.
`Metrics.Write` holds the registry mutex across the client write; a slow admin scraper stalls every request-path `Inc`.
`refill()` re-anchors `last` backwards on a backwards clock, so the next forward call mints tokens for the rewound interval (over-admission after an NTP step).
Tenant eviction scans at most 64 map entries per admission; when those are active/recent, requests get 429 `tenant_cap` even though evictable buckets exist beyond the scan window.
`s.fail` collapses all 4xx to `safeStatusMessage`, so specific messages such as `errTenant` ("tenant query parameter is required") reach clients as "invalid request".
`config/env-flags.json` is wholly re-indented (168→490 lines) in this change: ~40 real new flags are buried in pure churn and formatting-tool conflicts become likely.

Per-request upload buffering (up to 64 MiB in `ParseMultipartForm` plus a full `io.ReadAll` copy) × global concurrency 10 ≈ 1.3 GiB transient; pre-existing pattern, now codified as the supported limit.
NIT: `failures` in `RoleGuard.RecheckLoop` is incremented/reset but never read by any decision or metric.
`server.dsn` and `withStore`'s unused `ctx` parameter are dead after the shared-pool change.
Weak-token list only matches the whole token, so a ≥24-char variant of a known weak value passes (length is effectively the only production gate).
`fallbackWriter` re-enters `WriteError` for 404/405 (second encode whose body is discarded) — correct today, fragile for future middleware.
SUMMARY: Solid, well-tested guardrail package: envelopes, quotas with injected clock, fail-closed profile/role checks and shared-pool usage are largely in line with the AC.
Top risks: an unresolved dependency on store-side APIs not present in this diff, AC drift on the shutdown drain and metrics contract, and a quota slot held during non-cancellable body reads.
Recommend resolving the store question, reconciling AC/docs/implementation defaults, and adding a drift test before merge.
